statement_record.book: A natural transformation θ : F → G is a natural isomorphism — an isomorphism in the functor category Fun(C,D) — exactly when every component θ_X : FX → GX is an isomorphism in D; and then: decide whether the analogous claim holds for monomorphisms, i.e. whether θ is monic in Fun(C,D) exactly when every component is monic.
statement_record.intree: Instance/Fun.v:255 — `Theorem Functor_Setoid_Nat_Iso `(F : C ⟶ D) (G : C ⟶ D) : F ≅[Fun] G ↔ F ≈ G.` with `≈` on functors unfolding (Theory/Functor.v:148) to a family of componentwise isomorphisms `∀ x, F x ≅ G x` satisfying the naturality equation `fmap[F] f ≈ from (iso y) ∘ fmap[G] f ∘ to (iso x)`; the two directions are also exported as `iso_equiv` (Instance/Fun.v:305) and `equiv_iso` (:308), and the ← direction builds the Fun-isomorphism whose `to` component at X is the given component iso.
statement_record.strength_comparison: iso clause: same content, mildly repackaged — the book predicates on a GIVEN θ ('θ is invertible iff each θ_X is'), the library states an existential equivalence between 'there is an iso in [C,D]' and 'there is a componentwise-iso family satisfying naturality'. That repackaging is faithful in this setoid setting (the ← direction consumes exactly the data of a natural transformation with invertible components and returns an iso whose to-component is that family), so the mathematical content of Awodey's Lemma 7.11 is in force. Mono clause: intree-weaker — no counterpart at all.

gap: Only the isomorphism half is formalized. The monomorphism half has NO in-tree counterpart: there is no statement that a natural transformation is monic in [C, D] iff each of its components is monic in D, in either direction (rg -n 'Monic|Epic' over Instance/Fun.v, Instance/Fun/Cartesian.v and Theory/Natural/Transformation.v returns 0 hits; rg -l 'Monic' over the tree lists only morphism-level files — Theory/Morphisms*.v, Structure/{Abelian,Kernel,Equalizer/Fork,SubobjectClassifier}.v, Instance/Sets*.v — none about functor categories). Secondarily, the iso half is stated existentially (F ≅[Fun] G ↔ F ≈ G) rather than as a predicate on a given transformation θ, so 'this θ is invertible' must be routed through equiv_iso rather than read off a dedicated lemma.

Program Definition Curried_Hom `(C : Category) : C^op ⟶ [C, Sets] := {| fobj := fun x => {| fobj := fun y => {| carrier := @hom C x y ; is_setoid := @homset C x y |}; fmap := fun y z (f : y ~{C}~> z) => {| morphism := fun (g : x ~{C}~> y) => (f ∘ g) : x ~{C}~> z |} |}; fmap := fun x y (f : x ~{C^op}~> y) => {| transform := fun _ => {| morphism := fun g => g ∘ op f |} |} |}.   (* notation [Hom A , ─] *)
Definition Curried_CoHom `(C : Category) : C ⟶ [C^op, Sets] := Curried_Hom C^op.   (* notation [Hom ─ , A ]: the presheaf Hom(−, c) : C^op ⟶ Sets, typed by C^op^op = C definitionally *)

statement_record.book: For a locally small category C there is a functor Hom : C^op × C → Sets whose partial functors are the representables: Hom(C,−) : C → Sets is the covariant representable and Hom(−,C) : C^op → Sets the contravariant one (hint: use the Bifunctor Lemma).
statement_record.intree: `Hom (C : Category) : C^op ∏ C ⟶ Sets` with fobj (a,b) the hom-setoid hom C a b and fmap f g = snd f ∘ g ∘ fst f (post-compose with the covariant component, pre-compose with the contravariant one); `Curried_Hom C : C^op ⟶ [C, Sets]` whose value at x is exactly the covariant representable y ↦ hom C x y with fmap = post-composition; `Curried_CoHom C : C ⟶ [C^op, Sets]` whose value at c is the presheaf Hom(−, c).
statement_record.strength_comparison: same, and in-tree-stronger in one respect: the two partial-functor families are packaged not merely as functors for each fixed object but as functors OF that object into functor categories (Curried_Hom / Curried_CoHom), which is more than the exercise asks; the file goes on to prove that packaging full and faithful (Yoneda_Full :96, Yoneda_Faithful :85). One presentational caveat: no lemma explicitly identifies Hom's partial functor at a fixed first argument with Curried_Hom's value there — the identification is by unfolding (Hom's action becomes snd f ∘ g ∘ id, equal to post-composition only up to id_right), since Curried_Hom is defined independently rather than derived from Hom by currying. The library also builds the bifunctor directly rather than via the Bifunctor Lemma (the hint), which is a proof-route difference only.
